report_title: International AI Safety Report 2026
finding: Voluntary safety frameworks remain dominant across all evaluated jurisdictions, with no jurisdiction having implemented binding pre-deployment safety requirements with enforcement mechanisms as of the report date.

report_title: International AI Safety Report 2026
finding: Reliable pre-deployment safety testing has become harder to conduct as AI capabilities increase, and an explicit evidence-action gap is acknowledged across evaluated jurisdictions.

report_title: An Evaluation Framework for AI Misuse in Fraud and Cybercrime
finding: Open-weight models with guardrails removed are substantially more harmful than aligned closed-weight models across fraud and cybercrime task evaluations, demonstrating that safety alignment provides meaningful protection and its removal creates material harm uplift.

report_title: Evidence for Inference Scaling in AI Cyber Tasks
finding: Recent frontier models productively use 10-50x larger token budgets than typical eval settings — ~8% of AISI's cyber tasks were solved only when the budget rose from 10M to 50M tokens.

report_title: Evidence for Inference Scaling in AI Cyber Tasks
finding: Standard AI safety evaluations using fixed token budgets systematically underestimate the true cyber capabilities of frontier models, meaning that deployment decisions based on such evaluations may rest on incomplete risk assessments.

report_title: Evidence for Inference Scaling in AI Cyber Tasks
finding: Average cost per run at 50M tokens was ~$10, with a maximum below $60; a 'cost per success' metric can identify the optimal inference budget.

report_title: How Do Frontier AI Agents Perform in Multi-Step Cyber-Attack Scenarios
finding: Scaling context from 10M to 100M tokens yielded up to 59% gains on multi-step cyberattack benchmarks with no plateau; at 100M tokens Opus 4.6 reached 15.6 steps vs Opus 4.5's 11.0, a 42% gain in about two months.

report_title: Large-Scale Red-Teaming Competition on AI Agent Security
finding: The red-teaming competition compromised every one of the 13 frontier models tested (100% rate), with agent hijacking and indirect prompt injection remaining unsolved across all systems.

report_title: Large-Scale Red-Teaming Competition on AI Agent Security
finding: The red-teaming competition involved over 400 participants who generated more than 250,000 attack attempts against 13 frontier AI models, representing the largest structured adversarial evaluation of frontier AI agent security to date.

report_title: Can AI Agents Escape Their Sandboxes? Container Breakout Benchmark
finding: Frontier AI agents frequently achieved container breakout in environments with common cloud misconfigurations, with all successful escapes exploiting previously disclosed CVEs rather than zero-days. report_title: How are AI agents used? Evidence from 177,000 MCP tools
finding: Analysis of 177,436 AI-agent (MCP) tools found that the share of state-changing 'action' tools rose from 27% to 65% of total usage over the 16-month period sampled, indicating rapid expansion of agents into consequential real-world actions; the report proposes oversight at the tool layer.

report_title: How are AI agents used? Evidence from 177,000 MCP tools
finding: Software development dominates the agent ecosystem: 67% of all agent tools and 90% of MCP server downloads.

report_title: How are AI agents used? Evidence from 177,000 MCP tools
finding: Tool taxonomy of perception / reasoning / action tools; most action tools are medium-stakes (e.g. file editing) but some enable higher-stakes operations such as financial transactions.

report_title: GPT-5.5 Biosecurity Evaluation (SecureBio with CAISI oversight)
finding: GPT-5.5 was the highest-performing or among a small handful of highest-performing models on static biosecurity knowledge assessment, exceeding all expert human scores.

report_title: SecureBio GPT-5.5 Pre-Release Assessment
finding: GPT-5.5 pre-release checkpoints scored 52.0% on VCT, 56.2% on MBCT, 64.7% on HPCT and 53.2% (second-highest) on WCB in SecureBio's biosecurity assessment, with a 23% refusal rate on screening-evasion tasks.

report_title: GPT-5.5 Biosecurity Evaluation (SecureBio with CAISI oversight)
finding: GPT-5.5 Checkpoint 2 scored lower on BioTIER safety than its predecessor, though SecureBio stated no clear conclusion can be drawn because safety classifiers were disabled for that assessment.

report_title: GPT-5.5 Biosecurity Evaluation (SecureBio with CAISI oversight)
finding: On ABC-Bench task-based evaluations, GPT-5.5 (Checkpoint 2) delivered strong performance matching or exceeding GPT-5.4 across fragment design, screening evasion, and liquid-handling tasks, with only a 23% refusal rate on screening-evasion tasks.

report_title: GPT-5.5 Biosecurity Evaluation (SecureBio with CAISI oversight)
finding: Gemini 3.1 Pro became the first frontier model to reach the 100th percentile of expert virologists on VCT, ahead of GPT-5.5 Checkpoint 2 which reached it second.
